what: The BSD Packet Filter paper (McCanne and Jacobson)
note: No code: the paper describes the machine Linux copied four years later, an accumulator, an index register and sixteen words of scratch memory.

what: Linux Socket Filter: classic BPF on one socket
note: Older than git, so the whole release is one patch against 2.1.74. Search it for net/core/filter.c (367 lines, new) and include/linux/filter.h (108).

what: classic filters translated into x86-64 machine code
note: A new directory, arch/x86/net. bpf_jit_comp.c turns each classic instruction into x86-64 bytes; bpf_jit.S holds the slow paths that load packet data.
subject: net: filter: Just In Time compiler for x86-64
author: Eric Dumazet

what: seccomp: classic BPF filters system calls
note: The filter reads a struct seccomp_data, the system call number and its six arguments, instead of a packet. kernel/seccomp.c grows by 396 lines.
subject: seccomp: add system call filtering using BPF
author: Will Drewry

what: eBPF: the machine rebuilt inside the kernel
note: The new instruction set and its interpreter, still inside net/core/filter.c. Classic filters are translated on load, which is why kernel/seccomp.c changes too.
subject: net: filter: rework/optimize internal BPF interpreter's instruction set
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: eBPF programs translated into x86-64 code
note: The 2011 compiler rewritten for the new instruction set: one switch over opcodes that emits x86-64 bytes, the shape reads.
subject: net: filter: x86: internal BPF JIT
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: the bpf() system call and maps
note: kernel/bpf/syscall.c is born with one command, BPF_MAP_CREATE. Lookups, program loading and the verifier came in the other ten patches of the series.
subject: bpf: introduce BPF syscall and maps
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: kprobes: a program on (almost) any kernel function
note: kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c is born: the first program type outside networking, attached through perf’s kprobe events.
subject: tracing, perf: Implement BPF programs attached to kprobes
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: tail calls: one program jumps to another
note: The program array lives in kernel/bpf/arraymap.c; the jump itself is a few lines in the interpreter in kernel/bpf/core.c. reads both.
subject: bpf: allow bpf programs to tail-call other bpf programs
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: bpffs: programs and maps pinned as files
note: kernel/bpf/inode.c is born: a small file system whose files hold a reference to a map or program, so either outlives the process that made it.
subject: bpf: add support for persistent maps/progs
author: Daniel Borkmann

what: tracepoints: fixed, named hooks
note: Nineteen added lines. Attaching to tracepoints reused the plumbing the kprobe commit of 4.1 had built.
subject: perf, bpf: allow bpf programs attach to tracepoints
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: XDP: a program in the network driver
note: A program type, its context struct xdp_md and the verdicts XDP_DROP, XDP_PASS and XDP_ABORTED. The driver hooks came later in the series.
subject: bpf: add XDP prog type for early driver filter
author: Brenden Blanco

what: bpf-to-bpf function calls
note: verifier.c learns where one function ends and the next begins. The stack-frame checks that make calls safe are the next patch of the series.
subject: bpf: introduce function calls (function boundaries)
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: BTF: the kernel describes its own types
note: kernel/bpf/btf.c is born, with the format in include/uapi/linux/btf.h. At first BTF described map keys and values; type information for the whole kernel came in 5.2.
subject: bpf: btf: Introduce BPF Type Format (BTF)
author: Martin KaFai Lau

what: the one-million-instruction limit
note: Three changed lines. The limit was a constant, and the work that made a larger one affordable came in the patches before it.
subject: bpf: increase complexity limit and maximum program size
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: bounded loops
note: push_insn() stops refusing every backward jump, and is_state_visited() learns to report an infinite loop when a state repeats on the same path.
subject: bpf: introduce bounded loops
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: CO-RE: compile once, run everywhere
note: The relocation algorithm in tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c, merged for 5.4. The compiler side shipped in Clang 10 in March 2020, the year CO-RE became usable.
subject: libbpf: implement BPF CO-RE offset relocation algorithm
author: Andrii Nakryiko

what: trampolines: programs on function entry and exit
note: kernel/bpf/trampoline.c is born, and the x86 JIT learns to write the trampoline itself, a small generated function that saves registers and calls the programs.
subject: bpf: Introduce BPF trampoline
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: struct_ops: BPF fills in a table of kernel callbacks
note: A kernel structure of function pointers whose entries are BPF programs, in kernel/bpf/bpf_struct_ops.c. sched_ext is built on it.
subject: bpf: Introduce BPF_PROG_TYPE_STRUCT_OPS
author: Martin KaFai Lau

what: bpf_link: an attachment becomes an object
note: struct bpf_link in kernel/bpf/syscall.c: an attachment gets its own file descriptor and can be pinned like a map.
subject: bpf: Introduce pinnable bpf_link abstraction
author: Andrii Nakryiko

what: LSM programs
note: Seventeen lines create the program type in kernel/bpf/bpf_lsm.c; the security hooks it attaches to arrived later in the series.
subject: bpf: Introduce BPF_PROG_TYPE_LSM
author: KP Singh

what: the ring buffer
note: kernel/bpf/ringbuf.c is born. The 195 changed lines in verifier.c make reserve-then-submit a rule the verifier enforces.
subject: bpf: Implement BPF ring buffer and verifier support for it
author: Andrii Nakryiko

what: sleepable programs
note: The trampoline wraps a sleepable program in rcu_read_lock_trace() rather than rcu_read_lock(), and verifier.c limits which programs and maps may sleep.
subject: bpf: Introduce sleepable BPF programs
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: kfuncs: programs call ordinary kernel functions
note: verifier.c learns to check a call to an ordinary kernel function against its BTF type, the check follows.
subject: bpf: Support bpf program calling kernel function
author: Martin KaFai Lau

what: BPF token
note: kernel/bpf/token.c is born: an object that lets a container load programs it could not load on its own capabilities.
subject: bpf: Introduce BPF token object
author: Andrii Nakryiko

what: arena
note: kernel/bpf/arena.c is born: memory shared by a program and a user process at the same addresses, with pages added on demand.
subject: bpf: Introduce bpf_arena.
author: Alexei Starovoitov

what: RFC 9669: the instruction set becomes a standard
note: No code: the instruction set written down as an IETF standard, based on the kernel’s own document.

what: sched_ext: a CPU scheduler written in BPF
note: kernel/sched/ext.c is born at 4,256 lines. The scheduler’s callbacks are a struct_ops, the 2020 row above.
subject: sched_ext: Implement BPF extensible scheduler class
author: Tejun Heo

what: signed BPF programs
note: BPF_PROG_LOAD checks a signature in kernel/bpf/syscall.c. Earlier patches of the series bind a map to one program by hash, so a signed loader can trust what it reads.
subject: bpf: Implement signature verification for BPF programs
author: KP Singh
